headline: Iran re-escalates with ballistic missile strike on US forces; oil surges ~4% overnight as markets brace for the Fed, Microsoft, and Meta on the same afternoon.
stance: Risk-off pre-market: equities flat-to-lower on geopolitical flare-up, oil leading the tape higher. Today stacks three simultaneous catalysts — the Fed's rate decision at 2pm ET (hold widely expected, but Chair Warsh's tone on September is the live question), then Microsoft and Meta earnings after the close. Positioning in S&P 500 futures is extended long (speculators heavily positioned — a contrarian warning), while Russell 2000 and SOFR futures sit at the opposite extreme — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for small-caps and rate bulls.

news.head: Iran fires ballistic missiles at US troops
news.body: The US military said it intercepted an IRGC ballistic missile salvo targeting American forces in the Middle East overnight, snapping a brief pause in hostilities and sending oil surging more than 4% in pre-market trade.

news.head: WTI back above $82 pre-market
news.body: WTI crude (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET) is quoted near $82.09/bbl and Brent near $86.97/bbl after the renewed attack, reversing the prior session's three-day slide and reigniting Strait-of-Hormuz supply-disruption fears.

news.head: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% expected today
news.body: The FOMC concludes its two-day meeting today with a hold at 3.50%–3.75% widely anticipated; markets will focus entirely on whether Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30pm ET signals that a September hike is on the table.

news.head: Microsoft and Meta report after the close
news.body: Microsoft and Meta both post Q2 results this evening — the market's main question for both is whether massive AI capital spending (Meta guided $125–145bn for 2026, Microsoft ~$190bn for its fiscal year) is translating into measurable revenue.

news.head: Ford surges ~4% after hours on earnings beat
news.body: Ford Motor jumped nearly 4% in after-hours trading on Tuesday after topping earnings expectations and raising its full-year 2026 outlook.

news.head: Semis under renewed selling pressure
news.body: The prior session saw chip stocks remain under broad pressure, with the semiconductor sell-off that began on reports of a Chinese chip-making breakthrough continuing to weigh on Nasdaq breadth.

implications: Oil re-pricing higher complicates the Fed's inflation calculus and raises the bar for any dovish pivot language from Warsh — a hawkish tone today could pressure long-duration assets and high-multiple tech.

The equity-credit correlation reading of 0.684 means stocks and credit spreads are moving together; any geopolitical shock that widens HY spreads (currently 281 bps over IG) is likely to hit equities simultaneously — limited natural hedge between the two.

The 10-year breakeven inflation expectation sits at 2.20% while the real 10-year yield is 2.41% — markets are not yet embedding a large energy-driven re-inflation premium, but another leg higher in oil could change that quickly.

Positioning: S&P 500 futures: speculators are heavily positioned long (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning. Russell 2000 futures: speculators have almost no bullish bets left (4th percentile) — a contrarian floor. 3M SOFR: extended short positioning (4th percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean on near-term rates. Copper futures: speculators are heavily positioned long (96th percentile) — a contrarian warning. Wheat futures: speculators are heavily positioned long (98th percentile) — a contrarian warning. Euro FX: speculators have almost no bullish bets left (10th percentile) — a contrarian floor for EUR.

watch.head: Fed statement & Warsh presser (2pm ET)
watch.body: Any language suggesting the FOMC is 'meeting-by-meeting' and that September is 'live' for a hike would likely lift the dollar, push 10Y yields toward 4.70%, and reprice rate-sensitive equities lower.

watch.head: Microsoft & Meta AI capex guidance
watch.body: Both companies reporting tonight must justify enormous AI spending — a reassuring capex-to-revenue narrative from Meta at 4:30pm ET sets the tone for Microsoft's call and the broader tech sector open Thursday.

watch.head: EIA crude inventory report
watch.body: Wednesday's EIA weekly crude stocks report could add or subtract from the overnight oil spike — a draw would confirm tight physical supply; a surprise build would moderate the geopolitical bid.

watch.head: USD/JPY at extreme levels
watch.body: The yen (PRIOR CASH CLOSE 163.79 ¥/$) is at the 99.9th percentile of its three-year range — a historically extreme level of yen weakness; any hawkish Bank of Japan commentary or risk-off shift could trigger a sharp yen strengthening move, with knock-on effects across carry trades.

watch.head: Nasdaq breadth divergence
watch.body: Only 46.5% of Nasdaq 100 stocks trade above their 50-day average (vs. 67.2% for the S&P 500) — a divergence that suggests the index-level calm masks deteriorating conditions under the surface in tech.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.61%; 2-year yield: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.26% — the curve (2s10s) sits at +35 bps, a modest positive slope after months of inversion, meaning bond investors are slightly more worried about the long run than the near term.

Real (inflation-adjusted) 10-year yield stands at 2.41% — a high level that makes equities expensive to justify on a pure income comparison: the stock market's earnings yield (inverse of valuations) must clear that hurdle to attract new capital.
10-year breakeven inflation expectation is 2.20% — still near the Fed's 2% goal, but the overnight oil spike risks pushing this higher if sustained.

Term premium (the extra yield investors demand for holding long bonds instead of rolling short ones) is 83.8 bps — elevated, and a sign that bond buyers are requiring more compensation for uncertainty, which puts upward pressure on mortgage rates and corporate borrowing costs.

Financial conditions (ANFCI -0.55 z-score, STLFSI -0.70) remain accommodative — easier than average — which is one reason the Fed has not felt urgency to cut; the Iran flare-up has not yet tightened conditions materially.

The Fed's balance sheet is growing only 1.35% year-over-year, and overnight Fed repo usage (the daily cash-parking facility) has nearly drained to $1.1bn — meaning excess cash in the banking system is being deployed, not hoarded.
sections.positioning: 3M SOFR futures: speculators have almost no bullish bets left (4th percentile, 3-year low) — a contrarian floor suggesting the market has over-priced rate-hike risk in the short end; any dovish Fed nuance today could trigger a sharp rally in short-term rate futures.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 7,428.78; S&P 500 futures indicated slightly lower OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET near 7,425 — equities absorbing the oil shock with limited panic so far.
Nasdaq 100: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 24,876.91 — chip-stock weakness and AI capex scrutiny kept the index marginally negative Tuesday while the Dow gained 1.03% on strong non-tech earnings.
Dow Jones: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 52,747.32 — the Dow's outperformance vs. Nasdaq reflects a rotation away from high-multiple semis toward more traditional industrials and financials.

VIX (fear gauge — measures how much investors are paying to insure against a market drop): PRIOR CASH CLOSE 18.21 — calm for now; VXN (Nasdaq-specific fear gauge) at 28.61 is notably higher, confirming tech-specific anxiety is elevated.
SKEW index at 143 — investors are paying a meaningful premium to protect against a large, sudden market drop, even as headline VIX looks modest.
67.2% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day average, and 69.1% above their 200-day average — broad market internals are healthy; the weakness is concentrated in mega-cap tech and semis.
CAPE (long-run valuation measure comparing current prices to 10-year average earnings): 40.57 — historically elevated, leaving little margin of safety if earnings disappoint or rates rise further.
sections.positioning: S&P 500 futures: speculators are heavily positioned long (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning. Russell 2000 futures: speculators have almost no bullish bets left (4th percentile) — a contrarian floor; small-cap shorts are heavy with meaningful squeeze risk if the Fed surprises dovishly or geopolitical news calms.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — company insiders have been buying, stock trades above its 200-day line, and active dark-pool and options flow are live; with semis under broad selling pressure, an insider-buying signal in the sector's dominant foundry is worth tracking for a potential divergence.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY-IG spread (the gap between what risky companies pay to borrow vs. safe ones): 281 bps — wide enough to signal some stress but not at crisis levels; investment-grade spreads at 81 bps are similarly contained.
Bank credit growth is running at 6.4% year-over-year — a healthy pace indicating banks are still lending, not pulling back.
Commercial paper funding spread (the cost for large companies to borrow overnight in the money market): 18 bps — benign; no signs of a funding squeeze.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads (measures of stress in short-term bank-to-bank lending) at 1 bp each — essentially zero, confirming interbank plumbing is clear.
Bank reserves at $3,062bn and TGA (Treasury's cash account) at $829.6bn — ample system liquidity; no near-term risk of a 'repo market seizure' like 2019.
M2 money supply growing 5.53% year-over-year — moderate, not inflationary on its own, but combined with an oil shock it adds to the inflation watch list.

single_name.note: Five Star Bancorp (FSBC) — two insider-buying rules fired, stock trades above its 200-day line, shorts are heavy at 5.69 days-to-cover with meaningful squeeze risk; a regional bank signaling insider confidence during a rate-uncertainty backdrop.
